- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply dampening factor to subsequent days.
- Forecast errors cluster near the end of the 30-day horizon; especially in last 5–7 days, true values often dip or stabilize — model should taper upward bias.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -0.50), model may lag in adjusting; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast decline.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.67), model tends to be overly optimistic; apply conservative bias downward by 1–3%.
- Model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion after 3–5 day peaks; add 1–2 day decay factor to peak forecasts.
